diagnosis.root_cause: shop-web became unhealthy because a Docker Compose operation stopped its database dependency, shop-db, and left it exited with code 0 while the web container kept running. With an unless-stopped restart policy, shop-db did not come back automatically, so web health checks and item requests failed to reach the database.

evidence.detail: Container state shows shop-db exited with code 0 while shop-web is running and unhealthy.
shop-web health checks began failing after it could not reach the database endpoint, then later could not resolve the database hostname.
Docker events show an explicit kill/stop/die sequence for shop-db around 11:34:55 with no subsequent start event.
shop-db exited cleanly, was not OOM killed, and has restart policy unless-stopped, consistent with an external stop rather than a crash.
Compose labels show shop-web and shop-db came from different worktree config files, suggesting separate compose contexts touched the same service name.

proposal.reason: The diagnosis says shop-web is unhealthy because its database dependency, shop-db, was stopped and left exited. Starting the stopped shop-db container is allowed by the human rule and should restore the database endpoint for web.

run.judge_reason: The diagnosis identifies shop-db as stopped and explains that shop-web cannot reach its database, matching the expected cause of the API failure. Its additional evidence about the Compose stop and restart policy is consistent and does not introduce a conflicting cause.

report.title: unhealthy on demo/compose:shop
report.summary: shop-web became unhealthy because its database dependency, shop-db, had been stopped and left exited while the web container kept running. Bleep investigated and proposed starting the stopped database container on demo. The human rejected the proposal on the dashboard, so no action was taken and nobody confirmed recovery.
report.cause: A Docker Compose operation stopped shop-db and left it exited under an unless-stopped restart policy, so shop-web could not reach its database dependency.
follow_ups: Check whether shop-db is still exited and start it manually if the service should be running.
Review the restart policy for shop-db so a stopped database does not stay down unintentionally.
Add monitoring that detects when a dependent container exits while its consumer remains running.
Confirm which Compose context or worktree owns shop-db to avoid separate configs affecting the same service name.
